benchmark_kind: real-dataset lossiness of the supported packed-scan backend on MetaQA
scope_warning: These are statistics extracted from PRIOR recorded runs in results/, not from a run performed now, and not from the raw knowledge graph, which is absent from this tree (data/ is empty). They establish how much the source-keyed fanout cap discards; they do NOT give the degree distribution or the per-owner volumes that a volume-hiding evaluation needs.

the_finding.reading: The supported packed-scan backend caps adjacency by SOURCE. On real MetaQA that discards 56.8% of the federated graph at fanout 2 and 35.5% at fanout 4. The mean degree is only 3.09, but 19% of (owner, source) pairs exceed 4, so the loss is driven by a heavy tail rather than by a uniformly high degree. That is precisely the distribution a source-keyed cap handles worst, and precisely what keying by (source, relation) is meant to narrow.

why_it_matters_here: Every earlier argument for the relation-paged layout used SYNTHETIC skew from scripts/build_skewed_fixture.py. This is the same argument on real data: the supported backend is not merely slower than it could be, it is lossy, and measurably so. The recorded regression results are bounded-reference matches against a capped graph, so they are consistent with the cap while the cap itself discards most of the edges.
what_this_does_not_establish: The maximum (source, relation) degree, which is what sets page_size and is still an ASSUMED value (16) in relation_page_cost_model.json.
The narrowing factor on real data, so the 17.5x crossover measurement remains synthetic.
Per-owner data volumes, so the volume-hiding motivation is still argued rather than measured on a real federation.
Anything measured now; these are extracted from prior recorded runs.
Any result for the relation-paged backend on MetaQA, which has never been run.
what_would_close_the_gap: The raw MetaQA knowledge graph. With it, doram_t2_3pc/capacity_planning.py already computes the degree profile, the lossless bounds, and the per-owner key counts directly; prepare_scan plan-capacity is the entry point. That single input would convert three of the five items above from assumed to measured.
